To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the contents of phytochemical compounds in fruits/berries are regulated by environmental factors, which vary in different plant genotypes, growing periods and environmental factors.
the contents of sugars and acids in fruits and berries depend on the genetic background of the plants and are closely correlated with environmental changes during growth.

sugars and organic acids in fruits and berries were regulated by various environmental factors, including light intensity, temperature, and water supply, and that these factors might interact with each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of primary metabolites in relation to environmental variation, which is an important aspect of plant physiology and plant-microbe interaction.
the regulation of the composition and nutritional quality of fruits and berries by variation of environmental conditions and their interaction with genetic background.
the regulation of phytochemical composition in fruits and berries, especially the primary metabolism, in response to environmental variation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the contents of sugars and acids in fruits and berries were determined by the complex interactions between the genetic background and environmental factors, which could be utilized in the cultivation and breeding of fruits and berries.

the contents of sugars and acids in fruits and berries are closely correlated to environmental conditions, and the influence of environmental changes depends largely on the genetic backgrounds of plants.

the influence of environment on fruits/berries is very complicated and depends on the interaction of multiple factors, and it is necessary to take into consideration the interaction between the environmental factors and the genetic background of the plant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in general, the environmental conditions during fruit development affect the contents of sugars and malic acid in fruits and berries, and this impact depends on the plant genotype as well as on the interaction between environmental factors.

environmental factors, such as temperature, light intensity, and water supply, are important factors influencing the content of sugars and organic acid in fruits and berries, and the regulation of these compounds in relation to environmental changes depends on the interaction between environmental conditions and the genetic background of the plants.
the composition of fruits and berries is closely related to environmental variation, but the regulation of the composition is also dependent on plant genotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for fruits and berries with a high level of sugars and/or organic acids, the contents of these compounds are positively correlated to light intensity and negatively correlated to water supply.

the environmental variation during growth has a significant impact on the composition of fruit/berries, and that the regulation of the primary metabolites in response to the environmental changes is closely correlated to the genotype of plants as well to the developmental stage of fruits/berries.

the contents of sugars and acids in fruits and berries are closely related to the environmental conditions and plant genotype, and the regulation mechanism varies between different species, cultivars, and growing conditions.
